query: Lifecycle marketing has been sending win-back emails to at-risk users for the last two quarters, chosen by hand from a dashboard. They want me to build a churn model on our user table so we can (a) pick who gets the email better and (b) show leadership the emails work: users the model flags as high-risk who got an email churned 9 points less than flagged users who didn't. Can you sketch the model and the analysis for the deck?
expected_behavior: Separates the two asks. Takes (a) as a targeting decision made continuously at volume and scopes it as a model, noting that who-gets-the-email is an uplift question, not a propensity one, and that uplift needs randomised rows the hand-picked campaign did not produce. Refuses (b): the 9-point gap is self-selection (marketing chose whom to email, and the model learns that targeting and reports it back as risk), and a model's predictive accuracy is not evidence of the emails' effect. Routes the impact claim to an experiment: randomise the email across the eligible population with exposure logged, with the current hand-picking as the control, and says that readout, not any offline model metric, is what goes in the deck and the prior store. Without the skill, the model typically builds the churn model and reports the 9-point gap with caveats about controls, or proposes a regression with covariates as the impact analysis.
